question.problem:
Let $X$ be a random variable with the probability density function shown below. What are the modes of $X?$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{(2-x)(x+1)^{2}}{8}, & -2\le x\le 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The modes of a random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ are the values of $x$ at the global maxima of $f(x).$

To find the global maxima of $f(x),$ we find the critical points of $f(x)$ and then apply the candidates test.

First, we find the critical points.

- The piece of $f(x)$ defined on $-2\le x\le 2$ is $f(x)=\frac{(2-x)(x+1)^{2}}{8}.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{-(x+1)^{2}+2(2-x)(x+1)}{8} \\  & =\frac{(x+1)(-x-1+4-2x)}{8} \\  & =\frac{3(x+1)(1-x)}{8},\end{aligned}
$$

and solving ${f}^{′}(x)=0,$ we get

$$
\frac{3(x+1)(1-x)}{8}\,⟹\,x=-1,1.
$$

All of these critical points are within the interval $[-2,2],$ so we keep them all.

- The derivative doesn't exist at the endpoints $x=-2,2.$ So, these are critical points as well.

Now, we evaluate $f(x)$ at the critical points $x=-2,-1,1,2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =\frac{(2+2)(-2+1)^{2}}{8}=\frac{1}{2} \\ f(-1) & =\frac{(2+1)(-1+1)^{2}}{8}=0 \\ f(1) & =\frac{(2-1)(1+1)^{2}}{8}=\frac{1}{2} \\ f(2) & =\frac{(2-2)(2+1)^{2}}{8}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compare all of the values above. The largest values are

$$
f(-2)=f(1)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the modes of $X$ are $-2$ and $1.$
